summary: Architecture policy for product applications that have outgrown single-folder simplicity but do not need platform-grade ceremony.
description: A portable architecture pack for small-to-mid product applications with multiple features, user workflows, runtime integrations, and enough shared behavior to need explicit boundaries.

appliesWhen.summary: The project has several feature areas or user workflows that change independently.
evidence: Multiple feature, route, or domain directories

appliesWhen.summary: The project has shared API, persistence, auth, job, storage, or integration code that many features consume.
evidence: Cross-feature imports into helpers or service wrappers

appliesWhen.summary: The project needs more than one validation lane but does not need a large-platform governance program.
evidence: UI or integration smoke tests are present or planned
Release checks are slower than daily local checks

avoidWhen.summary: A one-off script, spike, or throwaway prototype should not inherit mid-app structure.
A library package with public API compatibility as its main concern should use a library architecture pack instead.
evidence: Semver migration policy dominates feature layout

avoidWhen.summary: A modular platform with strict package boundaries, generated routes, DI, and multi-team ownership needs a large-platform pack.

rules.title: Composition root owns runtime wiring
rules.summary: App startup, route registration, dependency assembly, provider selection, and environment interpretation must live in a composition root or platform layer, not inside feature internals.
rules.rationale: Feature code stays testable and portable when runtime choices are assembled at the edge.
examples: src/platform/** exposes stable runtime adapters consumed by features
antiPatterns: Feature service imports environment variables directly
Route handlers select providers ad hoc

rules.title: Feature owns product behavior
rules.summary: A feature should own its user workflow, domain service, screen-level UI, validation, and local tests unless the behavior is genuinely cross-feature infrastructure.
rules.rationale: Agents can make coherent changes when the behavior they need is locally discoverable.
antiPatterns: Business decisions hidden in shared helpers
Feature UI spread across unrelated global component folders
Tests only at a distant app level

rules.title: Shared code is earned
rules.summary: Shared modules must represent stable cross-feature primitives, platform adapters, or design-system components. Do not create shared buckets for speculative reuse.
rules.rationale: Premature shared folders make agents choose generic placement and create second patterns.
examples: src/support/formatting/money.ts after two or more features need identical money formatting
src/platform/api/client.ts as a single API boundary
antiPatterns: One feature imports another feature's private helper

rules.title: Import direction is one-way
rules.summary: Feature internals may depend on platform/support primitives, but platform/support code must not depend on feature internals, and features must not import private internals from sibling features.
rules.rationale: Acyclic direction keeps refactors bounded and makes ownership clear.

rules.title: Public surface is explicit
rules.summary: Feature entrypoints, route handlers, app APIs, and reusable components should expose intentional public files instead of encouraging deep imports.
rules.rationale: Explicit surfaces let agents and humans change internals without breaking unrelated callers.
antiPatterns: Exporting every file through a barrel by default

rules.title: Boundary data is validated
rules.summary: External input should be parsed at transport, persistence, job, and integration boundaries before it reaches feature logic.
rules.rationale: Feature code should work with known shapes; uncertainty belongs at the edge.
examples: Route parses request body before calling feature service
antiPatterns: Repeated unknown coercion inside domain logic
Components defensively handle every possible server shape

rules.title: Validation lanes are declared
rules.summary: Projects should declare fast local checks, targeted feature checks, and slower release checks so agents know what proof is proportional to a change.
rules.rationale: Without lanes, agents either over-run expensive checks or under-prove risky work.
examples: typecheck and unit test as fast lane
E2E and build as release lane
Feature-specific commands listed in project docs
antiPatterns: Only one broad CI command is documented
Agent must guess which test proves a UI or API change

rules.title: Generated artifacts have owners
rules.summary: Generated files must name their source or generator and should not be hand-edited as a shortcut.
rules.rationale: Generated drift is one of the fastest ways for agents to create confusing false truth.
examples: Generated docs point to the source command
AGENTS.md names generated paths and regeneration command
antiPatterns: Generated folder has no ownership or refresh command
